questions.question: Why must deployment promotion require the previous environment to pass a health check?
choices: It makes the deployment process take longer, which is safer
Promoting unhealthy code to the next environment spreads the problem further
Health checks are only needed in production
It's a legal requirement for all cloud deployments
questions.explanation: If staging is unhealthy and you promote to production, you're knowingly deploying broken code. Health checks at each stage ensure problems are caught and fixed before reaching users.

questions.question: What should a rollback operation return?
choices: Just a boolean indicating success or failure
The previous version, success status, and a descriptive message
A new deployment ID for the rolled-back version
The full git diff between versions
questions.explanation: A rollback should return structured information: whether it succeeded, what version was restored, and a human-readable message. This helps incident responders understand what happened.

questions.question: Why is tracking deployment history important?
choices: It makes the deployment manager look more complete
It records every environment transition so you can answer 'when did this version reach production?'
History is required for database migrations only
questions.explanation: During incidents, you need to know exactly when a version moved through each environment. History tracks every transition with timestamps, enabling root cause analysis and audit trails.
